In the Fulham Nursery there is a full-grown treeof the old Lucombe oak, as well as one of the Fulham oak, of bothof which portraits are given in our last Volume, which strongly dis-play the characteristic difference between the two trees. The ageand origin of the Fulham oak are unknown; but Mr. Smithers, anold man who has been employed in the Fulham Nursery from hisyouth, and who remembers the tree above 45 years, says thatit always went by the name of the Fulham oak, and that he under-stood it to have been raised there from seed. We have examinedthe tree at its collar, and down to its main roots, several feet underground ; and, from the uniform texture, and thick corky characterof the bark, we feel satisfied that it is not a grafted tree.
